results.test: user sees the correct total including discount and VAT
results.fixerReasoning: The app charges VAT on the full subtotal: vat() in public/cart.js computes 1398 × 0.21 ≈ 294, when it should compute (1398 − 140) × 0.21 ≈ 264. Business rule 3 in the header of public/cart.js and the precondition in the test case both say VAT is charged after the discount, so the test is right and the app's vat() does the wrong thing. Subtotal and discount match the expected values, which shows the setup and locators work; only the VAT calculation is wrong.
results.fixerReport: Application bug in public/cart.js, in the vat() function. It sets `const taxable = subtotal(items);`, which applies 21% VAT to the full subtotal before the discount. The documented rule (rule 3 in the file header, and the test-case precondition) says VAT is charged on the amount the customer pays, after the discount. For keyboard plus monitor stand (subtotal 1398, discount 140) the app shows VAT 294 and total 1552. It should show VAT 264 and total 1522, so customers who qualify for the discount are overcharged by 30 here. In general the overcharge is 21% of the discount. The test is correct and has been left failing on purpose. Suggested app fix, which a developer should review rather than the test pipeline: in vat(), change the taxable amount to `subtotal(items) - discount(items)`. After that, total() automatically becomes (subtotal − discount) + VAT on the discounted amount. Separate issue, not the cause of this failure: data/products.json lists the desk mat (id 4) at 349, but the test 'user sees the catalogue price of a product' and its test case expect 299. That is reference-data drift and a human needs to decide which price is correct.

results.test: user sees the whole catalogue once it has loaded
results.fixerReasoning: The app is paging the catalogue on purpose. public/index.html renders the first four products straight away and adds the fifth 1500 ms later. The comment there says "The catalogue is now paged: the tail arrives after the first render", and the test case doc for this test says the last rows can arrive late. The test waits a fixed 100 ms and then counts once with `count()`, which never waits, so it always sees 4. The app and the data both have five products. The test's timing assumption is the problem, so the fix is an assertion that keeps retrying until five rows are shown, not a longer sleep.
results.reviewerReasoning: The other agent's claims check out. public/index.html (commit 972e9ae) renders the first four products and adds the fifth with setTimeout(..., 1500), the test case doc says the last rows can arrive late, and data/products.json still has five products, so neither the app nor the data is broken. The diff replaces a fixed 100 ms sleep and a one-shot count() with Playwright's web-first toHaveCount(5), which waits for the page to reach the required state; it is not a blind retry or a longer sleep. It keeps the exact count of 5 and doesn't touch the timeouts, config or app code. I couldn't run the test myself because the run was blocked at the permission prompt.
reviewerConcerns: toHaveCount uses Playwright's default 5 s expect timeout, which comfortably covers the 1500 ms delay, but the test would start flaking if the paging delay ever rose near 5 s.
